Skjær gulrøttene i staver. Legg dem i en mikrobølgesikker bolle med ca. 2 ss vann og dekk med en tallerken. De kokes i mikroen mens du lager sausen.
Rens de grønne bønnene og sett til side.

Når kyllingen tas ut, settes fyllet inn. Hell først den varme kyllingkraften jevnt over fyllet – det skal være fuktig, ikke bløtt. Stek udekket i ca. 15 minutter, rør halvveis. Blir ikke toppen sprø, kan du grille den i 2–3 minutter.
Når kyllingen er ferdig, legger du den på et skjærebrett og pakker den i folie. La den hvile mens du lager saus, bønner og gulrøtter.

Sausen: Sett langpannen på platen på middels lav varme. Hell i 2,5 dl varm kyllingkraft og rør til stekesjyen løser seg opp. Rør ut maisennaen i 1,5 ss varmt vann i en kopp. Tilsett maisennablandingen og rør godt. Rør innimellom til sausen tykner (2–3 minutter). Tykner den ikke, rører du ut litt mer maisenna og tilsetter. Smak til med salt og pepper. Hell over i en sausenebbe.
Mens sausen kobler seg, forveller du bønnene i kokende vann i 2–3 minutter til de er knallgrønne og møre. Hell av og vend inn smør og hvitløksinfusert olje.
Kok gulrøttene i mikroen i 2–3 minutter på full styrke til de er møre. Hell av.
Skjær opp kyllingen. Server med ovnsgrønnsakene, smørdampede bønner, gulrøtter, sprøtt brødfyll og hjemmelaget saus.

title: Svinekjøttboller med sitrongress og koriander (lavFODMAP)
description: Disse lavFODMAP kjøttbollene av svin med sitrongress og koriander er et enkelt måltid hele familien vil like!
ingredients: 2 ss fersk sitrongress, renset og hakket*
En skvett nøytral olje (riskli-, raps- eller solsikkeolje)
23 g fersk ingefær i tynne strimler
ca. 340 g pak choi, vasket og snittet
ca. 240 g gulrot, skrelt og i tynne staver
ca. 260 g langkornet hvit ris eller basmatiris (ukokt)
instructions: Finhakk korianderen og vårløken. Fjern de grove ytterlagene på sitrongresset og finhakk den myke kjernen. Skrell ingefæren og skjær i tynne strimler. Skrell og skjær gulroten i tynne staver. Grovsnitt pak choien (både blader og stilk). Sett til side.

Visp egget i en liten bolle. Ha svinekjøttdeig, koriander, sitrongress, chiliflak, brunt sukker, glutenfritt griljermel, hvitløksinfusert olje og egg i en stor bolle. Krydre med salt og pepper. Bland godt med hendene. Rull til små boller (ca. 6 per porsjon). Legg på mikrobølgesikre tallerkener.
Kok risen i en stor kjele etter anvisningen på pakken.
Sett kjøttbollene i mikroen, én tallerken om gangen. Kjør hver tallerken på full styrke i ca. 1,5 minutt. Da blir bollene gjennomkokte inni.
Varm nøytral olje i en stor stekepanne eller wok på middels varme. Stek kjøttbollene til de er gylne på alle sider og gjennomstekte.

Når kjøttbollene er ferdige, woker du grønnsakene: Sett pannen på høy varme. Ha i sesamolje, ingefær, gulrot og vårløk, og stek til det dufter (1–2 minutter). Tilsett pak choi, soyasaus og vann. Wok i 1–2 minutter og server straks med kjøttbollene og risen.

title: Nudelsalat med mynte og lammekoteletter (lavFODMAP)
description: Lammekoteletter passer til alle årstider og er nydelige sammen med lavFODMAP mynte- og urtepesto og risnudler i en smakfull salat.
ingredients: 1 ss nøytral olje (riskli-, raps- eller solsikkeolje)
ca. 280 g appelsin, skrelt og i terninger
instructions: Til mynte- og urtepestoen: Grovhakk mynten, ruccolaen og basilikumen. Ha alt i en blender eller et stavmikserbeger sammen med den hvitløksinfuserte oljen, majonesen, sitronsaften, tofuen og paprikaen. Kjør glatt. Smak til med salt og pepper.
Kok risnudlene etter anvisningen på pakken. Hell av, skyll med kaldt vann og la dem renne av igjen. Ringle over olivenolje, ha i pestoen og vend inn ruccola og mynte.

Mens nudlene koker, gjør du klar lammekotelettene: Gni dem inn med olivenolje, salt og pepper. Stek dem i en stor panne på middels høy varme i ca. 4 minutter per side, til kjøttet er rosa inni. La dem hvile i 5 minutter før servering.
Skrell appelsinene og agurken. Skjær appelsinene i terninger og agurken i tynne skiver delt i fire. Bland sammen.
Server lammekotelettene med nudelsalaten og appelsin- og agurksalsaen ved siden av.

title: Kokosnudler med chilikylling (lavFODMAP)
description: Denne asiatisk-inspirerte lavFODMAP-retten er superenkel å lage, og den laksa-aktige sausen har en frisk smak av sitron og kokos med et lite hint av chili.
ingredients: 1 ss fersk sitrongress, renset og finhakket*
120 g rød paprika, uten frø, i strimler
instructions: Skjær kyllingfileten i tynne strimler og sett til side. Fjern ytterlagene på sitrongresset og finhakk kjernen. Finhakk vårløken, vask og grovhakk pak choien, skrell og skjær gulrøttene i staver, og fjern frøene og skjær paprikaen i tynne strimler. Sett til side.

Legg kyllingstrimlene i en stor kjele og dekk med kaldt vann (tilsett mer vann om kyllingen ikke er helt dekket). Ha i sitrongresset og ingefæren. Kok opp, skru ned til middels lav varme og la det trekke i 5–10 minutter til kyllingen er hvit og gjennomkokt. Dette blir kraften i retten. Behold kraften og ta ut kyllingen – sett den til side.

Mens kyllingen koker: Legg risnudlene i en bolle og hell kokende vann over. La dem stå i ti minutter før du heller av, eller kok etter anvisningen på pakken. Skyll nudlene i varmt vann, la dem renne av og vend inn en skvett sesamolje så de ikke klistrer seg sammen.

Ha chilien, fiskesausen og pak choien i kraften. Fiskesausen lukter ganske skarpt – ikke mist motet! Lukten forsvinner når kokosmelken kommer i, og det smaker fantastisk. Kok kraften i ca. 2 minutter før du tilsetter kokosmelken, kyllingen og nudlene. Varm i 3 minutter til, eller til kyllingen er gjennomvarm. Smak til med mer chili om ønskelig.
Mens retten gjør seg ferdig, varmer du en stor stekepanne på middels høy varme. Wok gulrotstavene og paprikaen i to–tre minutter til de er møre.
Server kokosnudlene med de wokede grønnsakene, og topp med vårløk og peanøtter (om ønskelig).

title: Biffwok med lime og sesam (lavFODMAP)
description: Denne raske og enkle lavFODMAP biffwoken har en frisk limevri kombinert med asiatiske smaker.
ingredients: 500 g tynnskåret biff/schnitzel uten panering, skåret i supertynne skiver på tvers av fibrene
2 store lime (revet skall – ta vare på saften)
1 ss nøytral olje (riskli-, raps- eller solsikkeolje)
instructions: Skjær biffen i tynne skiver på tvers av fibrene. Riv limeskallet med et fint rivjern – bare det grønne laget, ikke det hvite under. Skjær brokkolien og bønnene i småbiter. Finhakk vårløken. Legg biffen i en middels bolle og tilsett limeskall, soyasaus og sesamolje. La det marinere mens du koker nudlene.

Kok risnudlene etter anvisningen på pakken i saltet vann (ta dem opp 1–2 minutter tidlig så de ikke blir overkokte). Ha brokkolien og bønnene i nudelvannet de siste to minuttene. Hell alt i et dørslag, avkjøl under varmt vann og la det renne godt av. Mens nudlene koker, rister du sesamfrøene i en liten tørr panne på middels varme under stadig omrøring – ta dem av når de begynner å brunes. Sett til side.
Vask og strimle spinaten.

Varm den nøytrale oljen i en stor wok eller stekepanne på høy varme og wok biffen i 1 minutt. Tilsett fiskesausen, vannet og spinaten og wok i ett minutt til. Ha i de avrente nudlene, bønnene, brokkolien, vårløken og de ristede sesamfrøene. Vend rundt på høy varme i 1 minutt. Ta av varmen og bland inn limesaften.
Server straks med et par omdreininger sort pepper og salt om ønskelig.

title: Krydrede kyllingklubber (lavFODMAP)
description: Disse lavFODMAP krydrede kyllingklubbene har masse smak uten å være for sterke! Retten er også god med lavFODMAP-grønnsaker etter sesong.
ingredients: ca. 700 g potet, skrelt og i biter
ca. 300 g kabochagresskar ELLER søtpotet, skrelt og i biter
En skvett nøytral olje (riskli-, raps- eller solsikkeolje)
ca. 240 g gulrot, skrelt og i staver
instructions: Forvarm ovnen til 180 °C (over-/undervarme). Skrell og skjær poteten og gresskaret (eller søtpoteten) i biter og legg i en langpanne. Ringle over nøytral olje og vend så grønnsakene er godt dekket. Krydre med salt og pepper. Gjør så klar kyllingklubbene.

Bland lønnesirupen og den hvitløksinfuserte oljen i en liten bolle. Bland de tørre krydderne (koriander, gurkemeie, sennepspulver, paprika, spisskummen, nellik og sort pepper) i en annen bolle. Smør bunnen av en langpanne med olje og legg kyllingklubbene i. Ringle sirup- og oljeblandingen over kyllingen og gni den inn. Dryss krydderblandingen over klubbene til de er godt dekket. Det kan bli litt krydder til overs – det er greit.
Stek kyllingklubbene og grønnsakene i ca. 45 minutter, til grønnsakene er sprø og kyllingen gjennomstekt. Vend grønnsakene en gang eller to underveis.
Skjær gulrøttene, brokkolien og bønnene i småbiter. Sett en middels kjele med vann til koking ti minutter før servering. Forvell grønnsakene i 2–3 minutter til de har frisk farge og er møre.
Server kyllingklubbene med de ovnsbakte potetene og grønnsakene.

title: Fisk med chili- og kokosskorpe (lavFODMAP)
description: Chili- og kokosskorpen gir denne lavFODMAP-fiskeretten en spennende og deilig vri på klassisk pannestekt fisk.
ingredients: 460 g mild hvit fisk (torsk, hyse, sei, lyr)
ca. 55 g colby- eller cheddarost, eller vegansk ost (valgfritt), revet*
1 ss nøytral olje (riskli-, raps- eller solsikkeolje)
150 g agurk, skrelt og i biter
140 g salat (smørsalat, isberg), vasket og strimlet
65 g rød paprika, uten frø, i terninger
instructions: Til chili- og kokosskorpen: Ha kokosmassen i en liten bolle og dekk med vann. La den trekke i 10 minutter og hell av. Fjern frøene fra chilien og finsnitt den. Finsnitt vårløken og kaffirlimebladene. Varm halvparten av sesamoljen i en stor stekepanne på middels høy varme og stek vårløk, chili og limeblader til det er gyllent og dufter (skal se karamellisert ut). Tilsett kokosen og stek i ett minutt til. Sett til side.
Ha resten av oljen i samme panne og stek halvparten av potetene til de er gylne og møre. Gjenta med resten. Krydre med salt og sort pepper.
Gjør klar salatingrediensene og skvis sitronsaft over.

Spray en middels stekepanne med olje og stek fisken i 2 minutter, snu og stek i 1–2 minutter til den er gjennomstekt. Legg fisken på et stekebrett, topp med revet ost og dekk med chili- og kokosskorpen. Grill i ovnen på høy varme i 1–2 minutter til skorpen er gyllen.
Server med potetene og salaten.

title: Rustikk kylling saagwala (lavFODMAP)
description: Denne kylling saagwala-retten er spesielt tilpasset slik at vi som spiser lavFODMAP kan nyte den uten mageproblemer.
ingredients: 1 mild grønn chili, uten frø, finhakket
instructions: Skjær kyllinglårene i biter. Brun dem i den hvitløksinfuserte oljen i en stor stekepanne på middels høy varme. Ta dem ut og sett til side.
Grovsnitt purren. Grovhakk spinaten. Fjern frøene fra chilien og finhakk den.
Stek purren, spisskummen, nelliken, gurkemeien og ingefæren i samme panne. Det blir en klumpete pasta. Ha i den grovhakkede spinaten og la den falle sammen i 2 minutter.
Tilsett tomatene og chilien og rør godt. Legg kyllingen tilbake i curryen og la den småkoke i 20–25 minutter til kyllingen er gjennomkokt. Hold lav til middels varme så curryen ikke svir seg.
Smak til med en klype sukker og noen omdreininger salt og pepper.
Server med ris, forvellede grønne bønner og grillet aubergine.

title: Low FODMAP Blueberry Crumble Slice
description: This blueberry crumble slice is just so yummy – no one will be able to tell it’s low FODMAP, gluten and dairy free!
ingredients: 422.53521126761 g gluten free self raising flour*
250 g butter or dairy free spread*
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350ºF) bake function. Grease a 20 x 30cm (20 cm by 30 cm) baking pan. If you want you can line the pan with baking paper.

Place 1,9 dl of sugar, 7,5 dl of gluten free self rising flour, salt and ground cinnamon into a medium sized bowl. Mix well. If using guar gum (or xantham) then add it now. The gum will help the mixture be less crumbly but you don't have to use it. Mix the gum through the dry ingredients.

Lightly beat the egg in a small bowl. Place the dairy free spread (olive oil spread or butter) in a bowl and soften slightly in the microwave (you want it soft to touch but not melted). Pour the soft dairy free spread spread and the egg into the dry ingredients. Blend using a fork until the wet ingredients have absorbed into the dry ingredients. Then rub the mixture between your fingers until it turns into quite large moist crumbs.
Pat half of the mixture into the pan. It needs to be pressed in firmly until the dough forms a smooth layer.
Add the blueberries evenly to the baking pan until they cover the dough. In a small bowl mix together the 3 ts of corn starch and 0,6 dl of sugar. Then evenly sprinkle the sugar mixture on top.
Crumble the remaining dough over the blueberry mixture.
Bake in the oven for 30 minutes or until top is slightly golden. Let the slice cool before cutting it into 15 pieces. Serve warm with a side of low FODMAP icecream. This slice also freezes well.

title: Low FODMAP Decadent Dark Chocolate Mousse
description: This low FODMAP chocolate mousse has a beautiful creamy texture and you only need a small portion to get your chocolate fix!
ingredients: 250 g firm tofu (weigh after draining the water)*
59.970014992504 ml low FODMAP milk (we used a 15 ml tbsp)*
instructions: Break the dark chocolate into chunks and place in a small saucepan with the white sugar and low FODMAP milk. Heat over low heat and mix continuously until the chocolate melts and the sugar dissolves. The chocolate mixture should have a dark silky smooth and slightly shiny look with no traces of un-dissolved sugar.
Drain the tofu and place in the food processor container with the double blade. Blend until smooth. Then add the melted chocolate mixture and blend until evenly mixed through.

Scoop the mixture into four small bowls, ramekin dishes, or cupcake holders. Place in the fridge to cool. The flavour of the mousse changes and deepens as the tofu cools (do not serve this mousse warm).
Serve cold with a platter of low FODMAP fruit like banana and oranges.

title: Low FODMAP Dark Chocolate Dipping Sauce
description: This decadent Low FODMAP dark chocolate dipping sauce is perfect for BBQs and hot summer afternoons.
ingredients: 87.719298245614 g dark chocolate (GF or DF if needed) (roughly chopped)*
1 ss butter or dairy free spread*
instructions: Roughly chop the dark chocolate.

Melt the dark chocolate, white sugar, and dairy free spread (olive oil spread or butter) in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring continuously. Then whisk in the low FODMAP milk until the chocolate sauce is smooth. Taste the sauce and add more white sugar if needed.
If you are restrained enough not to consume the sauce all at once, store it in the fridge and reheat it in the microwave.

title: Low FODMAP Sweet Chilli Sauce
description: I love sweet chilli sauce so decided to create a simple and easy recipe that is FODMAP friendly!
instructions: Sterilise a glass jar by washing with hot soapy water and then air dry the jar in the oven at 120ºC (250ºF) for 20 minutes.
Measure out 50g (50 g) of the red chillies. Coarsely chop the whole red chillies and add them to the food processor.
Halve and deseed the remaining 200g (200 g) of red chillies. Roughly chop them and add them to the food processor. Add 1,3 dl of white vinegar and process until the chillies are finely chopped.

Transfer the chilli mixture to a medium sized saucepan and add the white sugar and the rest of the white vinegar. Heat on low until the sugar dissolves. You will need to stir the mixture and this step should take about 5 minutes.

Then increase the heat to high and bring the mixture to a boil. Reduce heat to medium and allow the sauce to simmer for 20 to 25 minutes or until the sauce thickens, stirring occasionally. The sauce should continue to thicken as it cools.
Pour into the sterilised air tight jar and seal. Store in the refrigerator for up to 3 months.

title: Simple Low FODMAP Cranberry Sauce
description: Cranberry sauce is a delicious Christmas condiment that goes perfectly with chicken, pork and turkey! I have used dried cranberries to make a low FODMAP sauce.
ingredients: 1,5 ts corn starch (dissolved in cold water)*
instructions: Place the dried cranberries in a large bowl. Pour over boiling water until they are completely submerged. Cover the top of the bowl with clingfilm to keep the steam in. Leave to soak for 20 to 30 minutes, until the cranberries have rehydrated and are soft.
Zest the orange (the trick is to only zest the bright orange layer and not the bitter white layer underneath).

Drain the cranberries using a sieve (they should now weigh about 225g or 225 g). Transfer the cranberries to a blender/food processer or use a stick blender and then add the cranberry juice. Process until reasonably smooth (a few chunky bits of cranberry are okay).

Place into a small saucepan and add the sugar, orange zest pinot noir wine and a pinch of salt. Dissolve the corn starch in a small amount of warm water and add to the saucepan. Place over medium low heat and allow the sugar to dissolve and sauce to reduce slightly until thick (this will take about 5 minutes), stirring occasionally. Once the sauce is your desired consistency remove it from the heat.

Place in a small bowl and pop into the fridge to chill. Make sure you divide the sauce into 12 serves to stay within the low FODMAP serving size for dried cranberries. This is about a tablespoon per serve. Store in the refrigerator.

title: Low FODMAP Virgin Piña Colada
description: Need a drink to have as a treat? Virgin piña coladas combine the delicious flavours of banana, coconut and pineapple to create a refreshing low FODMAP drink!
ingredients: 190.47619047619 g banana (firm - no brown spots) (slice & freeze in advance)*
instructions: Cooking Tip: Prepare the sugar water in advance and have it waiting in the fridge. That way you won't have to wait for the sugar water to cool when you are ready to have your refreshing drink.

Make the sugar water. Place the white sugar and water into a small saucepan. Stir until the sugar dissolves. Bring the water to the boil. Remove from heat and transfer into a container. Place in the fridge or freezer to cool. While the sugar water cools, cube the pineapple.
Place the coconut milk, sugar water, frozen banana, vanilla essence, and cubed pineapple in a blender. Blend until smooth.
Place a few pieces of cubed pineapple with some crushed ice into four glasses. Divide the mixture between the glasses. Garnish with fresh mint and cubed pineapple pieces if desired.
Serve immediately.

title: Low FODMAP Chocolate Millet Porridge
description: I am a self-confessed chocolate addict, and this low FODMAP chocolate millet porridge satisfies my cravings while keeping breakfast healthy.
ingredients: 1 medium banana (firm - no brown spots) (about ⅓ of a banana per serving)*
instructions: Cooking Tip: To make mornings easier, you can cook the millet in advance and reheat it with low FODMAP milk in the morning (see cooking notes).

Toast the millet seed in a saucepan over medium high heat, for about 2-3 minutes until it starts to go golden. Add the low FODMAP milk and boiling water. Throw in a pinch of salt. Then cover and bring to a simmer. Then turn down the heat to the lowest setting and allow to simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, until most of the liquid absorbs and the millet is soft.
Peel and slice the banana, and cut the strawberries into quarters.

Once the millet is cooked you can then stir through more low FODMAP milk until it is creamy. Stir through the unsweetened cocoa. Divide between bowls and top with the strawberries, banana and a drizzle of pure maple syrup. Enjoy!

Notes for cooking millet the night before: Complete step one in the method. Store the millet in an air tight container in the refrigerator. In the morning break up the millet using a fork. Transfer to bowls and add your low FODMAP milk. Heat in the microwave until warm. Then stir through the cocoa powder and low FODMAP fruit. Drizzle with maple syrup.

title: Low FODMAP Crispy Roasted Potatoes
description: These delicious low FODMAP crispy potatoes make the perfect side for breakfast or dinner. They are low FODMAP and super easy to make.
ingredients: 4 ss butter or dairy free spread*
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190ºC (375ºF) bake function.
Wash and dry the potatoes as needed. Then thinly slice the potatoes into 0.30cm (0,5 cm) thick slices.

Melt the dairy free spread (olive oil spread or butter). Brush the bottom of a 25cm (25,5 cm) oven proof frypan with 1 ss of the spread. Stack the potato pieces in the frypan in an upright position (not flat on the bottom - see feature photo).
Brush with the remaining spread and sprinkle with the fresh thyme (or rosemary), sea salt and black pepper, and chilli flakes (optional).
Place in the oven and bake for 1 hour. Remove once the potato is tender and edges are golden and crispy. Allow to cool for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Low FODMAP Chocolate Zucchini Cake
description: My low FODMAP chocolate zucchini cake is a favourite among my friends. Just remember that this cake is a treat food, so you need to watch your portion size!
ingredients: 250 ml neutral oil (rice bran, canola, sunflower)
1,5 ss boiling water (for the chia seeds)
281.69014084507 g gluten free all purpose flour (for best results weigh out the flour)*
100 g butter or dairy free spread*
20.993701889433 g dark chocolate (GF or DF if needed) (grated)*
instructions: Preheat the oven to 175ºC (350ºF) on bake function. Grease and line a 25cm (25,5 cm) round tin with baking paper.

Weigh and then grate the zucchinis. If you have a food processor you can use the grating blade to grate them. Gently squeeze the water out of the grated zucchinis using your hands. Place to one side for later.

In a cup place 2 ts of chia seeds and 4 ts of boiling water, then mix until soft (this will help the cake hold together). In a large bowl or using a food processor (use the double blade), mix together the oil, brown sugar, chia seed mixture, cocoa powder ground cinnamon, salt, and eggs until well combined and smooth. Then mix through the baking soda (dissolve it in 1 ss of warm water first).
In a large bowl mix together the gluten free all purpose flour and baking powder. Mix to combine the wet and dry ingredients (I do this in a food processor). Then mix through the shredded zucchinis.

Spread the cake batter into the prepared tin. Place in the middle of oven and bake for 40 to 50 minutes, until the top is spongy. Check the cake is fully cooked by inserting a skewer into the center - if it comes out clean it is cooked. Remove from the oven once cooked and allow to cool.
Grate the dark chocolate or roughly chop it using a sharp knife. Place to one side.

Once the cake is cooled make the icing. Soften the dairy free spread (olive oil spread or butter) slightly but do NOT melt it! I do this by placing the dairy free spread (or butter) in the microwave on high for about 10 seconds. In a large bowl mix together the icing sugar, hot water, cocoa and dairy free spread (or butter) until it is smooth and spreadable. Add a little bit more hot water if the icing is too thick.
Use a knife to spread the icing on the cake, then sprinkle with grated dark chocolate. Cut the cake into 16 serves.

title: Low FODMAP Bacon & Egg Salad
description: This delicious low FODMAP bacon & egg salad is quick to make and each serve fits perfectly into a 500ml preserving jar (mason jar).
instructions: Place the eggs in a small saucepan of cold water. Bring the water to a boil over medium heat, allow the eggs to boil for 2 minutes, then turn off the heat and leave on the element for 10 minutes. Then remove the eggs and place in cold water. Peel once they have cooled, and slice into quarters. Allow to cool before putting into the mason jars if possible.
Cut the bacon into pieces. Then fry in a medium sized frypan over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes until crispy. Allow to cool before putting into the mason jars if possible.
Cut the tomato into small pieces. Peel and thinly slice the cucumber, then slice in half again.
Mix the mayonnaise and garlic infused oil together until smooth. Add a few grinds of black pepper.
Place the garlic infused mayonnaise in the jars first, followed by the tomato, cucumber, baby spinach leaves, hard boiled eggs, and then the bacon.
Take to work and enjoy! Keep the salads cool until you are ready to eat them.

title: Low FODMAP Chocolate Brownie Cupcakes
description: These low FODMAP chocolate brownie cupcakes are the perfect treat, moist and chocolaty and they pair beautifully with the simple vanilla butter icing.
ingredients: 125 g butter or dairy free spread*
140.84507042254 g gluten free all purpose flour*
100 g butter or dairy free spread*
1 Sprinkle with edible cake decoration pearls (GF if needed)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 170ºC (340ºF) bake function. Line a standard muffin tray with cupcake liners.

Roughly chop the dark chocolate. Place the dairy free spread (olive oil spread, or butter) and dark chocolate into a microwave proof bowl. Cook in the microwave on high for 15 seconds and then stir. Repeat the process until the chocolate is melted.

In a medium sized mixing bowl, place the eggs, soy protein milk (lactose free milk or milk alternative), and vanilla essence. Whisk until smooth. Then add the melted chocolate and butter mixture and whisk through.
In a large bowl mix together the gluten free plain flour, cocoa powder, brown sugar, salt, baking powder and baking soda.
Mix the wet and dry mixtures together until smooth. Then spoon into the cupcake liners.

Bake in the oven for 15 minutes and then check with a baking skewer. The tops should be starting to crack slightly and the skewer should come out relatively clean (no large chunks of wet mixture). If the cupcakes are not cooked place them back into the oven for a couple more minutes.
Remove from the oven once cooked. Leave in the muffin tray for five minutes before transferring to a wire cooling rack. Allow to cool before icing.

Once the cup cakes are cool, make the vanilla butter icing. Soften the dairy free spread (olive oil spread or butter) slightly but do not melt it. In a large bowl mix the dairy free spread, icing sugar, vanilla essence, and one or two drops of red food colouring. Mix together until smooth. If your icing is too dry and won’t mix into a smooth creamy icing, then add ½ a teaspoon of warm water and continue mixing (I didn’t need to do this). Then pipe the icing onto the cupcakes. Sprinkle with edible decorations if desired.
Enjoy! Remember to only have one cupcake per serve.

title: Low FODMAP Rhubarb Custard Cups
description: These delicious low FODMAP rhubarb custard cups make the perfect dessert or snack.
instructions: Weigh and then chop the rhubarb. Place the rhubarb and raspberries in a small saucepan and cover with warm water. Place over medium heat and bring to a gentle simmer. Allow to simmer for about 10 minutes or until the rhubarb is soft. Drain off most of the excess liquid using a sieve. Then return the fruit to the saucepan and mash.

While the rhubarb stews, make the custard. Check the directions on your custard powder box and adjust the following directions as needed. Here is how I made my custard: place the custard powder, low FODMAP milk, and white sugar into a large microwave proof bowl. Whisk until smooth. Then whisk in the rest of the low FODMAP milk. Cook in the microwave on high for 2 minutes, then stir, cook in 1 to 2 minute increments until the custard is thick (stir after each time period). Taste the custard and stir through the vanilla essence if needed.
Layer the low FODMAP muesli, custard and stewed rhubarb into cups.
Serve immediately. Enjoy!

title: Rice Cakes with Chive Dip & Smoked Chicken
description: Looking for a tasty low FODMAP snack or light lunch? Rice cakes are a versatile low FODMAP food.
instructions: Make the chive dip by mixing together the garlic infused oil, chives and mayonnaise (or cottage cheese).
Slice the smoked chicken, dice the tomato and roughly chop the baby spinach.
Spread the dip onto the rice cakes and then add layers of baby spinach, smoked chicken, and diced tomato. Season with salt & pepper.
Enjoy!

title: Low FODMAP Gooey Chocolate Raspberry Desserts
description: These gooey chocolate raspberry desserts make the perfect low FODMAP Easter treat!
ingredients: 0,9 dl butter or dairy free spread*
70.422535211268 g gluten free all purpose flour*
0,5 ts chia seeds (or 0,5 ts xanthan or guar gum)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200ºC (400ºF) bake function. Line a muffin tray with 12 cupcake liners.

Break up the dark chocolate and place the pieces in a microwave proof bowl. Place in the microwave and heat on high for 15 seconds. Stir and then continue heating for 10 second increments (stirring each time) until the chocolate is melted. Alternatively melt the chocolate using a double boiler on the stove top.

Bring the dairy free spread (olive oil spread or butter) to room temperature (I heated mine for 5 to 10 seconds in the microwave). It should be soft but not melted. Place in a large bowl with the sugar and whisk until it is well combined, light and fluffy (I did this using a cake mixer on medium high speed for about 2 minutes). Then mix the eggs in, one at a time, until well combined.

Next beat in the gluten free all purpose flour and pinch of salt until smooth. Soften the chia seeds in boiling water. Add the melted chocolate and chia seeds (or add your xanthan or guar gum) to the bowl. Fold through until just combined.
Spoon half the mixture into the cupcake holders. Place 1 to 2 raspberries into the centre of each dessert. Then cover with the remaining mixture. Sprinkle with crushed raspberries.

Place in the oven and bake for 10 to 11 minutes. Remove as the sides start to crack and the top has just started to set (only the areas around the crushed raspberry should still be shiny). Allow to cool for 10 minutes in the muffin tray or on a wire rack before serving.
Remember to limit yourself to 1 mini dessert per serve. These are best served warm - you can reheat them in the microwave for a few seconds before serving. Enjoy!

title: Low FODMAP ANZAC Day Slice
description: Can't do oats? That's okay! This delicious low FODMAP ANZAC day slice is made using quinoa flakes instead of oats so you don't need to miss out.
ingredients: 211.2676056338 g gluten free all purpose flour*
180 g butter or dairy free spread*
1,5 ts baking soda (+ 2 ss boiling water)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180ºC (355ºF) bake function. Grease and line a 3cm (3 cm) deep, 19cm (19 cm) by 29cm (29 cm) slice pan with baking paper.
Place the gluten free flour, quinoa flakes, dried shredded coconut, pumpkin seeds, and sunflower seeds in a large bowl and mix well.
Next place the butter or dairy free spread, brown sugar, and golden syrup in a large saucepan over medium low heat. Stir occasionally until smooth. Then remove from heat.
Dissolve the baking soda in boiling water, then stir through the syrup mixture. It should go golden and frothy.
In a small cup, mix the chia seeds and boiling water, until the chia seeds soften and go gel like.
Add the chia seeds and syrup mixture to the dry ingredients. Mix well.
Transfer to the prepared pan. Using the back of a spoon, press the mixture evenly into the pan. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes or until golden brown. Allow to cool and then cut into squares.
Store in an airtight container for up to 5 days.

title: Minicrêpes med krydret kjøttdeig (lavFODMAP)
description: Trenger du en ny brunsj-idé? Prøv mine lavFODMAP minicrêpes med krydret kjøttdeig og sennepssaus.
ingredients: 2 ss smør eller melkefri margarin, smeltet*
ca. 240 g gulrot, skrelt og revet
instructions: Forberedelser: Lag crêperøren. Smelt smøret/margarinen. Visp eggene i en liten bolle. Ha smør, egg, melk, glutenfritt mel og salt i en stor bolle og visp glatt (eller kjør i blender).
Skrell og riv gulrøttene. Finhakk spinaten. Finsnitt purren. Åpne tomatboksen.
Start sennepssausen i en liten kjele: Visp sammen sukkeret og egget. Tilsett sennepspulveret, det glutenfrie melet, eddiken og kyllingkraften. Visp og sett til side.
Tilberedning: Du skal lage flere ting samtidig, så les gjennom stegene under før du begynner.

Sett en stor stekepanne på middels høy varme. Ha i nøytral olje, purre og kjøttdeig. Stek kjøttdeigen brun under omrøring. Tilsett halvparten av spinaten og gulroten (spar resten til servering), tomatene, de tørkede urtene (basilikum, oregano, timian) og worcestershiresausen, og krydre med salt og pepper. Bland godt. Skru ned til middels lav varme og la det småkoke mens du steker crêpene.

Stek crêpene: Varm en middels stekepanne på middels høy varme og smør den lett med oljespray. Hell ca. 0,6 dl røre i pannen og vipp den raskt rundt så røren dekker bunnen. Stek crêpen i ca. 2 minutter per side; snu når undersiden er lysebrun. Gjenta. Hold crêpene varme i ovnen. Røren gir ca. 8 små crêpes.
Mens crêpene og kjøttdeigen steker, lar du sennepssausen tykne i den lille kjelen på middels lav varme. Rør innimellom.
Server kjøttdeigen i crêpene med litt revet gulrot og spinat. Ringle sennepssausen over og pynt med litt basilikum.

title: Enkel lammegryte (lavFODMAP)
description: Denne enkle lavFODMAP lammegryten er varm og god – den perfekte lavFODMAP-oppskriften for vinteren.
ingredients: 1 ss nøytral olje (riskli-, raps- eller solsikkeolje)
ca. 240 g gulrot i små terninger
ca. 260 g kabochagresskar ELLER søtpotet, skrelt og i små terninger
ca. 320 g potet, skrelt og i små terninger
instructions: Smør slow cooker-bollen med matolje. Sett slow cookeren på lav.
Fjern fettet fra lammet og skjær det i terninger. Brun lammet i en stor stekepanne på middels høy varme i 4–5 minutter (kjøttet trenger ikke være gjennomstekt).

Ha lammet i slow cookeren. Grovhakk purren, og skrell og skjær gresskaret, gulroten og poteten i terninger. Ha alt i sammen med den hvitløksinfuserte oljen, oreganoen og timianen. Varm kraften og hell den i slow cookeren. Tilsett det kokende vannet. Krydre med sort pepper.
La slow cookeren stå på lav i 8–10 timer.
Sjekk gryten. Er kjøttet mørt, kan du mose gryten forsiktig med en potetstapper (det gjør den tykkere). Er gryten litt tørr, sper du med kokende vann til ingrediensene så vidt er dekket, og moser.
Rens bønnene, skjær dem i biter og forvell dem i kokende vann i 2–3 minutter til de er møre. Rør dem inn i gryten.
Rist det glutenfrie brødet. Grovhakk persillen.
Fordel gryten i boller og server med ristet brød. Pynt med fersk persille.

title: Low FODMAP Soothing Hot Lemon Ginger Drink
description: Winter is upon us in New Zealand and so many people are battling with colds or flu, so rug up with a mug of my soothing ginger and lemon drink!
ingredients: 125 ml pure maple syrup (you might need a little bit more)*
instructions: Wash and slice the lemon.
Peel and slice the ginger. If you love ginger then you can add more to your mixture if you desired.
Place the lemon and ginger into the glass jar in layers. Then pour over the maple syrup until the ingredients are covered.
Place in the refrigerator for at least 12 hours to allow the flavours to infuse.
Give the lemon ginger syrup a gentle mix (the maple syrup will settle to the bottom). Then scoop a spoonful into a mug and add hot water. Enjoy!
Over time the mixture might go a little bit jelly like and that's okay, just give it a quick stir before using. This syrup should keep for several weeks in the refrigerator.

title: Low FODMAP Curly Fries
description: Who doesn't love curly fries? These crispy morsels of golden potato make a delicious low FODMAP treat.
ingredients: 840 g potato (large, roasting variety like russet or white potatoes)
1 Drizzle of neutral oil (rice bran, canola, sunflower)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200ºC (390ºF) on bake function.
Peel the potatoes. Then transform the potato into spirals by running them through the spiralizer (use the larger triangular blade). Pat the potato curls dry.
Spread out the curly fries onto two baking trays lined with baking paper (don't overcrowd them).
Drizzle the curly fries with neutral oil.
Season with paprika, a few grinds of salt or pepper, and a pinch of dried chilli flakes (if desired). Toss to combine.
Place in the pre-heated oven and cook for about 20 to 25 minutes (or until the desired crispiness is achieved).
During the baking process, make sure to flip your fries and remove any pieces that have already crisped up, before placing the trays back into the oven.
Once your fries are crispy, remove the trays from the oven and serve immediately. The curly fries taste much better hot, and go great with a low FODMAP serve of tomato ketchup.

title: Low FODMAP Chicken Quinoa Meatballs with Teriyaki Sauce
description: This low FODMAP recipe makes a simple and delicious appetizer or main meal. Try adding some rice and low FODMAP vegetables for a tasty dinner.
ingredients: 20 g green onions/scallions (green leaves only, finely sliced)*
2 ss gluten free all purpose flour (as needed)*
instructions: Rinse the quinoa under running water using a fine mesh sieve for 40 seconds (this will help remove the bitter taste). Place the quinoa in a medium saucepan with the olive oil, and toast for 1 minute over medium high heat. Then add the water. Bring to a rolling boil. Turn down the heat to medium low and allow to simmer until cooked (about 12 to 15 minutes). Remove from heat once the quinoa is soft and the water has evaporated (you want it soft but not too wet).
Preheat the oven to 200ºC (400ºF) fan bake function.

While the quinoa cooks, finely chop the green onions/scallions (green tips only), and the fresh cilantro, and zest and juice the lime. Beat the egg in a small bowl. Place the ground chicken, green onions/scallions (green tips only), fresh cilantro, beaten egg, chilli flakes, ginger, sesame seeds, fish sauce, brown sugar, lime juice and zest into a large bowl. Add the quinoa once cooked. Season with a few grinds of salt and black pepper.
Then mix until well combined. If your mixture is a bit wet add a couple of tablespoons of gluten free flour and mix through. Using clean hands roll the mixture into small (walnut size) meatballs.
Place the meatballs on a large, lightly oiled baking tray or line it with baking paper. Bake in the oven for 18 to 20 minutes, or until all sides are golden and the meatballs are cooked through.

Make the sauce by mixing together the soy sauce, rice vinegar, garlic infused oil, ginger, sesame oil, and water in a small saucepan. Place the saucepan over medium high heat. Dissolve the corn starch in a little bit of warm water and then mix into the sauce. Allow to thicken for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring occasionally. Taste and add more brown sugar or rice wine vinegar if needed.
Serve the meatballs with the sauce and garnish with some green onions/scallions (green tips only) and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

title: Low FODMAP Lunchbox #1
description: Struggling to pack a low FODMAP lunchbox? Let me show you how to create a delicious and filling low FODMAP lunch!
instructions: Make a batch of spiced carrot & pumpkin muffins. These will last for several days in an air tight container or you can freeze and thaw the muffins as needed.
Make a batch of roasted red pepper & pumpkin hummus. This hummus will last for 5 to 6 days in the refrigerator.
Make the mustard mayo chicken salad the night before. It will keep for two days in the refrigerator.

Pack your lunch box with a portion of mustard mayo chicken salad (I like packing mine into glass jars), 1 spiced pumpkin & carrot muffin, 1 small banana, 2 to 3 ss of roasted red pepper with either veggie sticks (I like cucumber & carrot) or with plain rice crackers. Keep your lunch cool using ice packs or chiller pads.

title: Low FODMAP Salted Caramel Pumpkin Seeds
description: These salted caramel pumpkin seeds are highly addictive and make a great low FODMAP treat
ingredients: 1,5 ss butter or dairy free spread*
instructions: Preheat the oven to 150ºC (300ºF) bake function.
In a large bowl mix the pumpkin seeds, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and white sugar along with the water (you want the pumpkin seeds to be damp so the sugar and spices stick).

Line a large roasting tray with baking paper and grease with a little bit of cooking oil. Then evenly spread the pumpkin seeds across the tray. Place in the oven and bake for about 20 to 25 minutes until the pumpkin seeds are slightly golden and crunchy. Stir once while baking.

Just as the pumpkin seeds finish cooking, place a large saucepan over medium heat. Melt the butter or dairy free spread, then mix through the brown sugar, white sugar and salt. Allow to cook for 1 to 2 minutes until it is a deep golden brown, then turn down the heat to low. Gently mix pumpkin seeds through the salted caramel sauce until they are evenly coated. Then transfer the pumpkin seeds back into the roasting tray and allow to cool.
Enjoy! I love eating these as a treat or using them as a topping on ice cream, porridge or custard.

title: Low FODMAP Coconut Creamed Rice with Stewed Fruit
description: Low FODMAP coconut creamed rice makes a delicious hot breakfast or a yummy dessert, just add your favourite toppings to serve.
ingredients: 1 ss pure maple syrup (optional, to taste)*
1,5 ts pure maple syrup (a drizzle to taste)*
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160ºC (320ºF) bake function.
Place the rice, chia seeds, coconut milk, low FODMAP milk, water and cinnamon in a large oven proof dish. Mix well. Place in the oven uncovered.
Cook for 1 hour 30 minutes, stirring every 20 to 30 minutes to break up the skin that forms. Remove once the rice is thick and creamy like rice pudding.
Place to one side and allow to cool for a few minutes. Then taste and stir through the maple syrup if desired.

While the creamed rice cooks, make your stewed fruit. Wash the rhubarb stalks and chop into small pieces. Place the rhubarb and strawberries into a medium sized saucepan. Add the water and cover with a lid. Place over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until the fruit is soft and starts to collapse as you stir it. Taste and add a little bit of maple syrup if the mixture is too tart.
Serve the creamed rice with the stewed rhubarb and strawberries. Sprinkle with toasted pumpkin seeds if desired. Enjoy!

Storage & reheating tips: This creamed rice will cool and become quite solid. That's okay as it will soften when you reheat it. When reheating the rice, add an extra splash of milk to loosen the mixture before popping it into the microwave. Homemade creamed rice will last for 4 days when stored in an airtight container in the fridge.

title: Low FODMAP Garlic Infused Croutons
description: Low FODMAP garlic infused croutons are delicious! They are perfect on salads, dipped in soup, or simply eaten as a snack.
ingredients: 3 ss butter or dairy free spread*
instructions: If you are using fresh or frozen gluten free bread lightly toast it under the oven grill for a couple of minutes to dry it out before using. Stale gluten free bread is ideal for this recipe.
Preheat the oven to 170ºC (340ºF) bake function.
Melt the dairy free spread (olive oil spread or butter) and garlic infused oil in a covered bowl in the microwave (this will take about 10 to 20 seconds on high).
Cut the gluten free bread into 2 cm (2 cm) cubes.

Place the bread croutons into a bowl, and pour over the infused butter mixture. Toss the bread croutons until they are evenly coated then season with a sprinkle of oregano, and a couple of grinds of salt.

Spread the croutons in a single layer on a baking tray and place on the middle rack in the oven. Cook for 10 to 15 minutes, until golden brown and crisp. Turn once while they cook. Quick Tip: Don't leave these unattended in the kitchen! They can brown quickly so keep an eye on them and remove just as they go golden.
Enjoy the low FODMAP garlic infused croutons hot or cold. I love using them in salads, as a side for soup, or just as a snack!

title: Vegansk næringsbolle (lavFODMAP)
description: Denne lavFODMAP veganske næringsbollen («nourishing bowl») er en deilig lunsj eller middag!
ingredients: 1 mild rød chili, uten frø, grovhakket
ca. 360 g gulrot, skrelt og i terninger
ca. 260 g kabochagresskar ELLER søtpotet, skrelt og i biter
185 g hermetiske linser (veid etter skylling og avrenning)
1 klype chilipulver (valgfritt, sjekk at det er uten løk og hvitløk)*
3 ss fersk koriander, finhakket til pynt
instructions: Forvarm ovnen til 200 °C (over-/undervarme).
Ha den brune risen i en stor kjele. Tilsett grønnsakskraften og kok opp på middels høy varme. Skru ned til lav varme, legg på lokk og la det småkoke til vannet er absorbert (20–30 minutter).

Skrell og skjær gulroten og gresskaret i biter. Bland med olivenoljen, den røkte paprikaen og et par omdreininger salt. Legg i en langpanne. Bak i 25–30 minutter til de er gylne og møre. Snu én gang underveis.

Mens grønnsakene bakes, gjør du ferdig den grønne risen og krydrer linsene. Grovhakk spinaten, fjern frøene og finhakk chilien, og finhakk vårløken. Ha spinat, chili, vårløk, koriander, hvitløksinfusert olje og vann i blenderen. Kjør til en grov pasta og rør den inn i risen som koker.

Følg med på risen – slutter den å småkoke, skrur du opp varmen litt. Når vannet er absorbert, skrur du av varmen og lar risen stå i ca. 10 minutter. Rør den så luftig med en gaffel og smak til med salt og pepper.
Mens risen hviler, lager du de krydrede linsene og rister gresskarkjernene: Rist kjernene i en liten tørr panne i 2–3 minutter til de er lett gylne.

Skyll og la linsene renne av, og vei opp mengden du trenger. Ha dem i pannen på middels varme. Krydre med spisskummen og chilipulver. Tilsett vannet og la det småkoke i 4–5 minutter. Når vannet er fordampet, tar du pannen av varmen og tilsetter en skvis limesaft, salt og pepper. Sett til side.
Forvell de frosne edamamebønnene i kokende vann i 3–4 minutter til de er møre.
Server den grønne risen med de krydrede linsene, og topp med de ovnsbakte grønnsakene, gresskarkjernene, edamamebønnene og litt fersk koriander.

title: Low FODMAP Lunchbox #2
description: Looking for some low FODMAP lunchbox inspiration? Hot minestrone soup makes a yummy and filling lunch.
ingredients: 40 g colby, cheddar or vegan cheese (cut into cubes)*
instructions: Make the ANZAC slice over the weekend to reduce your work during the week. Store in an airtight container in the fridge to help it last longer.

Your minestrone soup can be made on Sunday and used over the next few days as lunch. Remember to slightly under cook your gluten free pasta to stop it from disintegrating when you reheat it. Each morning before you head off to work, warm your thermos with some hot water while you heat the soup, then drain the thermos and fill with soup.

If you want to get prepared you can pre-cut your cheese in advance and store the portions in snack size bags. That way you can just grab and go. If you don't want to use cheese, try my dairy free chive dip instead.
Cut the orange into segments and store in a small container or bag.
Pack your lunchbox with hot minestrone soup, a piece of ANZAC slice, crackers and cheese/dip, and an orange. Enjoy!

title: Low FODMAP Red Cabbage Sauerkraut
description: Low FODMAP red cabbage sauerkraut is fantastic for our gut as it is full of probiotics and soluble fibre, and is high in vitamins C & K.
instructions: Remove the outer leaves of the red cabbage. Remove the dense core of the cabbage and chop the cabbage into 1 cm (1 cm) strips. Then roughly dice.
In a large bowl toss the cabbage with the salt and allow it to sweat for 20 to 30 minutes. Mix through the caraway seeds.

Transfer the cabbage and any liquid into a clean 1 litre jar. Press down really hard with your fists, or use an implement, and pack each layer as tightly as you can. Hopefully you will notice some liquid starting to pool at the bottom of the jar. Leave for 30 minutes and then compress the cabbage. Do this twice. Hopefully enough liquid will leach out of the cabbage to at least half cover it. Then top the jar up with filtered water (no chlorine) until the cabbage is covered by at least 2.5cm (2,5 cm) of water.

Cover with a fermentation lid. You can't use a normal lid as the pressure in the jar may increase and cause your jar to explode! If you don't have a fermenting lid, 3/4 fill a snaplock bag with water (check it doesn't leak) and place on top of the jar. It should settle into the jar and seal it. Cover your jar with a tea towel and place somewhere dark that has an even temperature (like in a cupboard). If you get really stuck, you can cover the lid of your jar with clean cloth (make sure you tie it securely), which will keep the dust and bugs out.
Allow it to ferment for 10 days to 3 weeks. If you are in a colder climate or it's winter then you might need to let it ferment for a bit longer.
Taste the sauerkraut every few days. Once it gets a nice tangy flavor, place it in the refrigerator. It should keep in the refrigerator for up to two months.
Test your tolerance to a 1 ss serve then work your way up to a larger serving size. The largest serve you can enjoy on the low FODMAP diet is 1/2 a cup. Enjoy!

title: Burger med sprengt oksekjøtt og surkål (lavFODMAP)
description: Disse smakfulle lavFODMAP-burgerne med sprengt oksekjøtt og rødkålssurkål er perfekte som snacks eller lunsj.
instructions: Slik langtidskoker du sprengt oksekjøtt: Har du ikke ferdigkokt kjøtt, kan du koke det selv. Skyll kjøttet under rennende vann (jeg gjør det to ganger for å fjerne overflødig salt). Legg kjøttet i slow cookeren. Dryss over brunt sukker, nellik og sort pepper. Tilsett risvineddiken, laurbærbladet og gulroten (grovdelt i store biter). Dekk med 1–1,25 liter varmt vann. Kok på lav i 8–9 timer til kjøttet er mørt. Hell av og skjær opp.

Burgerne: Rist de glutenfrie burgerbrødene i ovnen. Riv gulroten. Legg salat, revet gulrot, kjøtt og rødkålssurkål (1–2 ss per burger) lagvis i brødene. Topp med en klatt grovkornet sennep og litt sort pepper. Ringle over majones om ønskelig.

title: Low FODMAP Curried Carrot & Chickpea Frittatas
description: These low FODMAP curried carrot & chickpea frittatas are one of my favourite snacks and a great way to sneak a low FODMAP serving of legumes into your diet.
ingredients: 49.019607843137 g butter or dairy free spread*
105.6338028169 g gluten free self raising flour*
40 g green onions/scallions (green leaves only, finely sliced)*
116.27906976744 g firm tofu (chopped into small cubes)*
166.66666666667 g canned chickpeas in brine (weight after draining & rinsing) (chopped into small cubes)*
instructions: Place the oven on to preheat at 180ºC (355ºF) bake function.

Place a large frypan over medium heat. Peel and dice the carrots into small cubes. Add to the frypan with a drizzle of olive oil. Allow to gently sautee for 10 to 15 minutes until soft and slightly golden brown. Stir occasionally.

While the carrot cooks, prepare the rest of the mini frittata ingredients. Melt the butter or dairy free spread. In a large bowl whisk together the eggs, low FODMAP milk, garlic infused oil, and melted butter or dairy free spread. Then whisk through the curry powder and gluten free self raising flour.

Finely chop the green onions/scallions (green tips only), grate the zucchinis, and roughly chop the fresh cilantro. Drain the tofu before chopping/crumbling into small pieces. Drain the chickpeas and rinse under cold water, before draining again.

Mix the grated zucchinis, green onions/scallions (green tips only), rinsed chickpeas, tofu, fresh cilantro and cooked carrot through the wet mixture. Season with a few grinds of salt and pepper, then mix again.

Line your muffin trays with paper liners (this will make clean up easier!), then spoon the mixture into the cups. Fill almost to the top. Place in the oven and cook for 25 to 30 minutes until springy and golden (if testing with a wooden skewer it should come out clean). Don't worry if your mini frittatas sink when they come out of the oven...that's normal and they will still taste delicious. These will keep in the fridge for two days or you can pop them into the freezer once they have cooled.
Reheating tip: Pop the mini frittatas in the microwave for 40 seconds to a minute (longer if reheating from frozen) to enjoy a warm snack.

title: Low FODMAP Halloween Pretzel Spiderwebs
description: These delicious dark chocolate & coconut pretzel spiderwebs make the perfect Halloween treat, The bonus is they only need 3 ingredients!
ingredients: 87.719298245614 g dark chocolate (GF or DF if needed) (roughly chopped for melting)*
instructions: Line a baking tray with baking paper. Then carefully break the pretzel sticks in half (you need 4 per spiderweb). Assemble the pretzels in a star pattern on the tray. Make sure you pop the broken pretzel ends to the middle of your star shape. Do this until you have the base for 12 spiderwebs.

Break up your dark chocolate. Place in a microwave proof bowl and microwave in 15 second intervals, until it melts (stir after each interval). Allow to cool for a minute and then transfer the dark chocolate into a resealable ziplock bag. Cut the very tip off one of the bag corners.

Gently squeeze the dark chocolate onto the pretzels. Start in the centre of your shape, until all pieces are connected, then drizzle the chocolate out in a circular motion to from the web. Sprinkle with finely shredded coconut.

Allow the chocolate to harden. If you are in a rush you can pop them into the freezer (make sure the tray stays flat) for 15 to 20 minutes. Then pop them off the tray using a flat spatular or knife. Store in an airtight container and keep cool. Enjoy!

title: Low FODMAP Pumpkin Pancakes
description: These low FODMAP pumpkin pancakes make a gorgeous brunch! They are fluffy and filling and go great with a side of bacon and banana
ingredients: 1,9 dl canned or fresh pumpkin puree (make fresh from Japanese pumpkin or Kabocha squash) (about 190 g / 190 g of raw pumpkin)
281.69014084507 g gluten free all purpose flour (for best results weigh the flour)*
2 ss neutral oil (rice bran, canola, sunflower) plus more for cooking
instructions: Preheat the oven to 50ºC (120ºF) bake function or use the warming function.

Make the pumpkin puree (if needed): Peel and deseed the pumpkin before chopping it into small bite-sized pieces. Place in a microwave-proof bowl or steamer with a couple of tablespoons of water. Cook on high in the microwave for 7 to 10 minutes (until the pumpkin is soft). Drain and allow to cool for a couple of minutes, before transferring the pumpkin into a blender container. Puree with a couple of tablespoons of water (add more if needed).

While the pumpkin cooks, place the gluten free plain flour, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, salt and brown sugar in a large bowl. Mix until well combined. In a separate bowl whisk together the low FODMAP milk, egg, and neutral oil. Once the pumpkin is blended, whisk through the wet ingredients.

Combine the wet and dry ingredients and mix until smooth. Homemade pumpkin puree can be a bit thicker than canned pumpkin puree, so if your mixture is a bit thick add another splash of low FODMAP milk.

Heat about a tablespoon of neutral oil in a large non-stick frying pan on medium heat. Use about 0,6 dl batter for each pancake and cook for 2-3 minutes on each side, or until pancakes are golden brown on both sides, and just cooked through. You should be able to cook about three at a time. Set aside on a plate and keep warm in the oven while you cook the remaining batter.
Serve hot with a side of grilled bacon, banana, toasted pumpkin seeds (or walnuts or pecans) and a drizzle of maple syrup.

title: Low FODMAP Ginger Halloween Cookies
description: These low FODMAP Halloween cookies are just so cute and are even better eaten iced.
ingredients: 125 g butter or dairy free spread*
316.9014084507 g gluten free all purpose flour (for best results weigh the flour)*
4 drop food colouring (blue, purple, or black) (add until icing looks the desired colour)
40 g dark chocolate chips (GF or DF as needed) (or chocolate gel writing pen)*
30 edible eyes (GF if needed - we bought these from a cake decorating store) - for the bats
instructions: Separate the egg white and yolk. Soften but do not melt the butter/dairy free spread.

Using a cake mixer, cream the spread/butter, sugar, golden syrup and maple syrup together until light and fluffy. Add the egg yolk and mix until just combined. Next, stir through the flour, ginger, cinnamon and cloves. After a couple of minutes of stirring, the dough should start to stick together and form chunks - if your batter is too wet, add another couple of tablespoons of flour.
Lightly flour the bench. Remove the dough from the bowl and knead until smooth. Wrap in plastic wrap and place in the fridge to chill for 30 minutes (do not skip).
Line 2 baking trays with baking/parchment paper.

Split the dough into 4 portions. Roll out each dough quarter between two pieces of baking/parchment paper (this will stop it from sticking to the bench and rolling pin). Once rolled, the dough should be about 5mm (0,5 cm) thick. Cut out the Halloween shapes and transfer them onto the baking trays. If any of the cookies split, gently mould them back together on the baking tray. Repeat this process until you have used all the dough.
Place the cut cookies in the fridge to rest for 10 to 15 minutes before baking.

While your dough rests, preheat the oven to 180ºC (355ºF) bake function. Then bake the cookies in the preheated oven for 8 to 10 minutes, until lightly golden. Allow them to cool on a wire rack (about 20 minutes).

Make the royal icing. Lightly whisk the egg white until light and frothy, then stir through the lemon juice. Slowly mix through the icing/powdered sugar until you have a smooth paste - you want it relatively firm but spreadable (if it becomes too thick - add a few drops of water). Divide your icing into two portions. Tint one portion using a few drops of food colouring. Then use piping bags to create the clean icing edge on your shapes, next fill the centre with more icing (smooth with a small spoon). Drop the edible eyes onto the bats as you go. Once the icing is set, draw on the ghost faces using a black food gel pen or melted dark chocolate.
Store in an airtight container.

title: Low FODMAP Coconut Macaroons
description: Coconut macaroons make a tasty low FODMAP treat, I love adding a little bit of lemon zest which brings out the vanilla and coconut flavours even more.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160ºC (320ºF) bake function and shift the wire rack into the bottom third of the oven.

Weigh out your shredded coconut. If it is very coarse you might what to chop it a bit finer. Then place in a roasting tray. Toast in the oven for 3 to 5 minutes. Turn the coconut once or twice, until it is lightly golden (just starting to colour), then remove. This will create a much deeper coconut flavour! Allow to cool slightly.
Zest the lemon and separate the egg whites. Then whisk the egg whites, sugar, vanilla, salt and lemon zest, until the egg whites and sugar are well combined, frothy, and white.
Pour the coconut over the egg white mixture and gently mix until the coconut is evenly moistened. Line a baking tray with baking paper.

Wet your hands before shaping the macaroons (this will help stop the coconut sticking to you). Shape the coconut into small balls about 3cm (3 cm) in diameter, and place them evenly on the baking tray (they will expand slightly so leave room).
Bake your macaroons in the oven for about 15 to 20 minutes, until golden.
Allow to cool for five minutes, before transferring to a wire rack. Then pop into an airtight container (they will last for up to a week).
Enjoy! Just remember to limit your serve to two macaroons at a time.

title: Glasert skinke (lavFODMAP)
description: Det finnes mange måter å lage en lavFODMAP glasert skinke på i høytiden – helt uten honning!
ingredients: ca. 30 hele nellikspiker (du trenger flere eller færre avhengig av rutemønsteret)
instructions: Forvarm ovnen til 150 °C (over-/undervarme). Flytt risten til nederste nivå. Kle en stor langpanne med to lag bakepapir. Legg skinken i pannen og sett den i ovnen i ti minutter (det varmer svoren og gjør den lettere å fjerne).
Mens skinken varmes, presser du appelsinene. Visp sammen lønnesirupen, det brune sukkeret, appelsinjuicen og dijonsennepen til glasuren.

Ta skinken ut av ovnen og øk temperaturen til 170 °C. Skjær et snitt rundt skanken med en skarp kniv (ca. 9 cm fra den smale enden). Før kniven under svoren langs kanten av skinken, og kjør deretter fingrene frem og tilbake mellom svor og fett for å løsne den. Da skal du kunne løfte av svoren i ett stykke. Kast svoren.
Rut fettet i et diamantmønster, ca. 5 mm dypt. Stikk en nellikspiker i midten av hver rute. Pensle med 1/3 av glasuren. Sett i ovnen.
Stek i 1 time og 30 minutter, og pensle med glasur hvert 25. minutt.

title: Low FODMAP Spiced Christmas Carrot Cake
description: Traditional Christmas cake is hard to make FODMAP friendly so I've created a delicious spiced carrot cake for my family to enjoy instead.
ingredients: 271.0843373494 g carrot (if possible use weight amount)
2 ts chia seeds (or 1 ts of guar gum or xanthan gum)
250 ml neutral oil (rice bran, canola, sunflower)
281.69014084507 g gluten free all purpose flour (for best results weigh the flour)*
197.36842105263 g gluten free confectioners sugar (powdered sugar)
1 Sprinkle with edible cake decoration pearls (GF if needed)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160ºC (320ºF) on bake function. Grease and line a 25cm (25,5 cm) round tin with baking paper.
Grate the carrots. If you have a food processor you can use that to grate them. Place to one side for later.
Place the dried cranberries and pumpkin seeds in the processor (with the double blade) and process until roughly chopped. Then place to one side.

In a cup place 2 ts of chia seeds and 3 ts of boiling water, then mix until soft (add another splash of water as needed - the chia seeds will help the cake hold together). In a large bowl or using a food processor, mix together the oil, sugar, chia seed mixture (if using guar gum or xanthan gum add it now), vanilla essence, and eggs, until well combined and smooth.

Add the gluten free all purpose flour, grated carrot, chopped cranberries & pumpkin seeds, salt, ground cinnamon, ginger, mixed spice and nutmeg to the large bowl. Mix to combine the wet and dry ingredients.
In a cup dissolve 2 ts of baking soda in 1 ss of freshly squeezed orange juice. Then mix through the cake batter.

Spread the cake batter into the prepared tin. Place in the middle of oven and bake for 55 to 60 minutes, until the top is spongy. Check the cake is fully cooked by inserting a skewer into the center - if it comes out clean it is cooked. Remove from the oven once cooked and allow to cool.

Once the cake is cooled make the icing. Separate the egg whites and whisk with the lemon juice. Shift the icing sugar into a bowl and then whisk for 5 to 10 minutes until it forms peaks. If your icing is too runny add more icing sugar and whisk well. Ice the cake immediately. Decorate with edible cake decoration pearls. Cut the cake into at least 16 serves.

title: Low FODMAP Traditional Hummus
description: Bet you didn't think traditional low FODMAP hummus was possible? Well, this recipe is going to blow your mind!
ingredients: 400 g canned chickpeas in brine (drain & rinse before using)
instructions: Drain and rinse the canned chickpeas under running water for 1 minute. Next shell the chickpeas (this will give you a smoother hummus - but you can skip this step). Gently pinch the skin of each chickpea to remove it.
Juice your lemon.
Add the tahini and lemon juice to the food processor or blender, and whip on high for 30 seconds, until well combined and smooth.

Then add the rinsed chickpeas, garlic infused oil, olive oil, water, cumin and salt. Blend until smooth. Blend through a little bit more water, if needed, until the hummus reaches your desired consistency.

Taste and add an extra squeeze of lemon juice if desired. Allow to chill in the fridge for 30 minutes then serve with your favourite meal or veggie sticks. You can also top the hummus with a sprinkle of paprika or some low FODMAP nuts or seeds if desired.
Enjoy! If you are in the first phase of the low FODMAP diet then limit your serving to 3 ss.

title: Low FODMAP Smoky BBQ Sauce
description: Are you excited yet?! You should be... this tasty low FODMAP BBQ sauce is super simple and you can create it in ten minutes.
instructions: Combine all ingredients in a medium sized saucepan. Bring the ingredients to the boil, then turn down the heat and allow to simmer for 5 to 8 minutes or until all of the brown sugar has dissolved.

Taste and add another pinch of cayenne pepper if you like it spicy! Now is the time to adjust the other flavours (Worcestershire sauce, apple cider vinegar, chives) to suit your taste preferences. If your sauce is too thin, you can thicken it using corn starch dissolved in a little bit of water, then simmer until the sauce is your desired thickness (I didn't need to do this).
Enjoy can enjoy up to 3 ss of this low FODMAP BBQ sauce per serve. This sauce will keep for a month in a sterilised jar in the fridge, or you can pop it into the freezer.
This sauce will keep for a month in a sterilised jar in the fridge, or you can pop it into the freezer.

title: Low FODMAP Strawberry Ice Cream with Fudge Sauce
description: Simple low FODMAP strawberry banana ice cream goes perfectly with chocolate fudge sauce, this is definitely a dessert your family will love!
ingredients: 200 g banana (firm - no brown spots) (freeze in advance)*
20 g dark chocolate chips (GF or DF as needed)*
2 ss butter or dairy free spread*
instructions: Chop the frozen banana and strawberries into small pieces. Place in a food processor with the coconut yoghurt, maple syrup and vanilla essence. Blend and scrape down the sides of the food processor as needed, until smooth (this will take 5 minutes or so).

Taste and add more maple syrup or vanilla essence if desired. Then serve immediately as soft serve (let's face it... I'm impatient and this is how I enjoy eating it) or freeze for a couple of hours until slightly firm.

Make the chocolate fudge sauce. Place the coconut milk, dark chocolate, cocoa powder, dairy free spread or butter, and maple syrup in a small saucepan. Place over medium heat and allow to melt, whisk occasionally. Let the sauce boil gently for 2 to 3 minutes until thick. Leave for a few minutes to cool and then spoon over the ice cream. Store any leftover sauce in a sealed container in the fridge.

title: Low FODMAP Banana Pecan French Toast
description: This lovely low FODMAP banana pecan french toast recipe is the perfect way to beat mid-week breakfast boredom.
ingredients: 0,5 ss butter or dairy free spread*
2 ss pecans (or toasted sunflower & pumpkin seeds) (crumbled)*
instructions: Place your large non-stick frypan on to warm over medium heat. Scramble the egg in a wide, flat bottomed bowl (think pasta plate) along with the cinnamon.
Place the gluten free bread one slice at a time in the egg, flip to cover entire bread. Make sure each of the slices soak up all the egg so none is leftover.
Add your butter or dairy free spread of choice to the frypan. Place the egg soaked bread into the pan and cook 2 to 3 minutes per side until slightly brown and toasty. Flip and cook the other side.
Serve on plate with a drizzle maple syrup, sliced banana, and a sprinkle of pecans (or toasted sunflower and pumpkin seeds).

title: Hjemmelagde burgere med BBQ-saus (lavFODMAP)
description: Alle elsker en god burger! Jeg serverer gjerne disse lavFODMAP-burgerne med BBQ-saus og en salat ved siden av.
ingredients: ca. 300 g gulrot, skrelt og i biter
1,5 ts nøytral olje (riskli-, raps- eller solsikkeolje)
140 g salat (smørsalat, isberg), vasket og strimlet
instructions: Forvarm ovnen til 210 °C (over-/undervarme). Skrell og skjær gulroten i biter, legg i en langpanne og vend i olje. Bak i 25–30 minutter til de er gylne og myke; snu én gang underveis.

Lag burgerne: Visp egget i en liten bolle. Bland kjøttdeig, finhakket vårløk, glutenfritt griljermel, tørkede urter (basilikum, oregano, timian), worcestershiresaus, vispet egg og noen omdreininger salt og pepper i en stor bolle. Form til like store burgere (2 per person).
Stek burgerne i panne eller på grillen på middels høy varme til de er gjennomstekte (ca. 7 minutter per side).
Mens burgerne steker, gjør du klar salaten: Vask og strimle salaten, skjær tomatene i skiver og agurken i tynne skiver. Rist burgerbrødene om ønskelig.

Sett sammen burgerne og topp med en klatt BBQ-saus. Bruk resten av salatingrediensene til en salat ved siden av, vend inn de ovnsbakte gulrøttene, og smuldre eventuelle ekstra burgere over salaten. Ringle over majones og BBQ-saus.

title: Low FODMAP Dark Chocolate Granola Recipe
description: I've been experimenting, and have created a low FODMAP & gluten-free dark chocolate granola recipe using quinoa flakes!
ingredients: 40 g coconut chips or dried shredded coconut*
115.78947368421 g dark chocolate chips (GF or DF as needed) (optional)*
instructions: Preheat the oven to 120ºC (250ºF) bake function.
Mix the dry ingredients in a large bowl (quinoa flakes/oats, chopped sunflower and pumpkin seeds, coconut chips, brown sugar, dutch cocoa powder, quinoa puffs or rice bubbles.
Mix the olive oil, vanilla and maple syrup together. Pour over the dry ingredients and mix well.

Evenly spread the granola mixture over two baking trays lined with baking paper. Bake in the oven for 20 minutes, then gently shake or stir the granola and bake for another 15 minutes. Then add the dark chocolate chips and a sprinkle of sea salt (to taste) and bake for another 5 minutes.
Let the granola cool for 1 to 2 hours. Then store in air tight jars or containers.
Enjoy a 1,3 dl serve as part of your breakfast or a snack! I love mixing mine with some coconut yoghurt and a serve of fruit.

title: Low FODMAP Grilled Pineapple with Yoghurt & Rice Cakes
description: Looking for a delicious low FODMAP snack? Grilled pineapple with low FODMAP yoghurt and rice cakes is the perfect option.
ingredients: 2 ss plain lactose free yoghurt (or coconut yoghurt)*
instructions: Cut the pineapple into chunks. Spray lightly with oil and grill in the oven on high for about 5 minutes per side. If you are feeling impatient, you can skip this step and just use raw pineapple.
Spread the coconut yoghurt or lactose free yoghurt onto the rice cakes, add the pineapple and sprinkle with chia seeds (optional). Enjoy!

title: Caramelised Banana with Low FODMAP Porridge
description: I love how caramelised bananas bring a lovely sweetness to this low FODMAP recipe, while the hint of cinnamon and vanilla give this breakfast a homely feel.
ingredients: 1,3 dl rice flakes or rolled oats*
125 ml low FODMAP milk (double the milk if using oats)*
2 ts neutral oil (rice bran, canola, sunflower)
instructions: Cook your porridge (rice porridge or oats) according to packet directions using the low FODMAP milk.

Heat a small saucepan over the medium heat. Add the neutral oil, maple syrup, a sprinkle of cinnamon and a dash of vanilla extract. Allow to bubble for a minute. Then add the sliced banana. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the banana is plump and golden.
Top the cooked porridge with the caramelised banana.

title: Low FODMAP Dark Chocolate Truffle Balls
description: With Easter just around the corner, these dark chocolate truffle balls make the perfect low FODMAP treat. You can adapt the toppings to suit your allergy needs.
ingredients: 0,6 dl gluten free plain or vanilla biscuit/cookies (crushed)*
4 ss sunflower & pumpkin seeds (toasted, finely chopped)*
instructions: Chop the dark chocolate into small pieces and place in a bowl with the coconut oil (melted), vanilla essence, and pure maple syrup.

Place the coconut cream in a small saucepan over low heat, until the milk starts to steam. Then pour into the bowl. Mix gently with a spoon until well combined and smooth (do not whisk - as this will incorporate air into the mixture).
Cover the bowl with cling wrap and allow to chill in the fridge for 4 to 5 hours (we need the truffle mixture to set).

Just before you roll your truffles, toast your desiccated coconut for 1 to 2 minutes over medium heat, until lightly golden. Remove the coconut and toast your pumpkin and sunflower seeds for 2 to 3 minutes until golden. Finely chop/crumble your desiccated coconut, toasted seeds, and vanilla biscuits (I used homemade). Place the desiccated coconut, toasted seeds, vanilla biscuits, and gluten free cocoa powder into separate bowls.

Line a tray with baking paper. Wash your hands in very cold water (the colder your hands, the easier it is to roll the truffles). Using a teaspoon, scoop out little truffle balls and roll in the palm of your hands, before placing them on the tray.
Then decorate by rolling the balls through your choice of toppings. Return the truffles to the fridge for 30 minutes to firm up before serving.
Storage: These truffles will last for a few days in the fridge.

title: Shepherd's pie (lavFODMAP)
description: Familien min elsker lavFODMAP shepherd's pie! Det har vært en av favorittmiddagene mine siden jeg var liten.
ingredients: 600 g mager lammekjøttdeig (eller kjøttdeig av storfe)
375 g lavFODMAP pastasaus med rødvin og italienske urter (f.eks. FODMAPPED)
ca. 90 g mangold (eller spinat/grønnkål), uten stilker, finhakket
ca. 1,2 kg potet, skrelt og i biter
ca. 60 ml lavFODMAP-melk (spe med litt ekstra ved behov)*
ca. 110 g colby, cheddar eller vegansk ost, revet*
ca. 240 g grønne bønner i biter
instructions: Forvarm ovnen til 200 °C. Smør en stor ildfast form.
Finhakk purren. Skjær gulrøttene i små terninger og finsnitt mangolden (eller spinaten/grønnkålen). Skrell potetene og skjær dem i småbiter.
Ha potetene i en stor kjele, dekk med varmt vann og kok i 15–20 minutter til de er møre.

Mens potetene koker, varmer du en stor kjele på middels høy varme. Ha i den hvitløksinfuserte oljen, purren og kjøttdeigen. Stek til kjøttet er brunet. Tilsett pastasausen, kyllingkraften, worcestershiresausen, gulrøttene og mangolden. Bland godt og skru ned til middels varme. La det småkoke i ca. 20 minutter under omrøring; ta kjelen av varmen når sausen har redusert. Rør inn basilikumen og smak til med salt og pepper.
Mos potetene med melken, smøret/margarinen, sennepen og noen omdreininger salt.
Ha kjøttblandingen i den ildfaste formen. Fordel sennepspotetmosen jevnt på toppen. Strø over revet ost om ønskelig.
Stek udekket i ovnen i 20–25 minutter til den er gyllen. La den hvile i fem minutter, og server med dampede grønne bønner.

title: Low FODMAP Berry Bliss Frozen Yoghurt Bark
description: There is nothing better than a frozen treat! My favourite at the moment is berry bliss frozen yoghurt bark made from low FODMAP yoghurt and berries.
ingredients: 312.5 g plain lactose free yoghurt (or coconut yoghurt)*
instructions: Line a small baking tray with baking paper. Chop the strawberries into small bite sized pieces.
Mix the vanilla extract through the yoghurt.
Spoon the yoghurt onto the baking tray and spread using a flat knife until the yoghurt is about 0.8cm (1 cm) thick. Make sure the yoghurt is thick enough to push the fresh fruit in.
Melt the strawberry jam, then swirl into the yoghurt using a spoon.
Sprinkle over the cut strawberries and whole blueberries, and then crumble raspberries over the top.
Freeze for 2 to 3 hours until hard. Cut using a sharp knife. Store in the freezer in an air tight container.

title: Low FODMAP Chocolate Coconut Fudge Sauce
description: I came up with this low FODMAP recipe for chocolate coconut fudge sauce... I promise you that this sauce will make any bad day better.
instructions: Place the cocoa powder, coconut cream, low FODMAP milk, vanilla essence, coconut oil and brown sugar into a blender. Blend for 30 seconds until smooth.

Place in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Bring to a boil and then allow to gently boil/bubble for 20 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes to stop it boiling over. Whisk in any skin that starts to form on the top (this skin should start forming towards the 15 to 20 minute mark and is how you know it will go fudgy in the fridge.

Place in the fridge and allow to cool for another 20 minutes. A thin skin will form over the sauce as it cools, just whisk it into the mixture. The sauce will continue to thicken as it cools and turn fudgy overnight.
Store in a glass jar in the fridge for up to 1 week. Recommended serving size is 1,5 ss as this recipe is heavy on the sugar. Enjoy!

title: Falafel (lavFODMAP)
description: Smakfull falafel, myk inni og sprø utenpå – et flott vegansk alternativ på lavFODMAP-dietten.
ingredients: ca. 165 g hermetiske kikerter i lake (veid etter avrenning og skylling)*
25 g fersk persille (mål opp, finhakk deretter)
instructions: Forbered falafelen: Varm den ferdigkokte brune risen. Riv gulroten og sett til side (kan gjøres i foodprosessor). Riv limeskallet og press saften, grovhakk persillen og det grønne av purren. Skyll og la kikertene renne av.

Ha alle ingrediensene i foodprosessoren. Kjør til en jevn masse (er den for tørr, tilsetter du en spiseskje vann). Rør deretter inn det glutenfrie melet (massen skal være akkurat tørr nok til å håndtere).
To måter å steke på:

I ovnen: Er du glad i sprø falafel, er dette alternativet for deg! Forvarm ovnen til 190 °C (over-/undervarme). Kle et stekebrett med bakepapir og smør det med 1 ss olivenolje (det gjør falafelen sprø). Mål opp falafel med en spiseskje og form små kaker. Fordel dem jevnt på brettet. Pensle toppen med en spiseskje olje. Stek i ca. 12 minutter per side til de er gylne.

I stekepannen: Liker du mykere falafel, prøver du denne metoden. Varm en stor slippfri stekepanne på middels høy varme og smør den med 1 ss olivenolje. Mål opp falafel med en spiseskje, form kaker og stek dem 2–3 minutter på hver side til de er gylne. Skru ned varmen om de begynner å svi seg, og tilsett mer olje ved behov. Legg dem på kjøkkenpapir. Stek i flere omganger.

Server med en lavFODMAP-dressing. Vår favoritt er hvitløksmajones: Bland sitron- eller limesaft med majones (bruk vegansk majones ved behov), sort pepper og en skvett hvitløksinfusert olje. Husk å dele falafelen i anbefalt antall porsjoner for å holde retten lavFODMAP (vanligvis 3–4 falafler per person).

title: Sprøstekt kylling med grønn karrigryte (lavFODMAP)
description: LavFODMAP grønn karrigryte høres kanskje litt rart ut, men det er kjempegodt – og en perfekt måte å bruke lavFODMAP grønn karrisaus på.
ingredients: 1 ts nøytral olje (riskli-, raps- eller solsikkeolje)
ca. 240 g gulrot, skrelt og i terninger
130 g rød paprika, uten frø, i biter
5 g fersk koriander, grovhakket til servering
instructions: Forvarm ovnen til 200 °C (varmluft). Lag marinaden ved å blande vårløken, limeskall og -saft, sukkeret, den hvitløksinfuserte oljen og den nøytrale oljen. Tørk kyllinglårene med kjøkkenpapir og legg dem i en stor bolle. Hell over marinaden og krydre godt med salt og pepper. Gni marinaden inn i kyllingen.

Kle en langpanne med folie og legg en rist i (har du ikke rist, går det fint – men kyllingen kan trenge litt lengre tid, og du må bruke bakepapir i stedet). Legg kyllingen på risten med skinnsiden ned og hell over resten av marinaden. Stek i ovnen i 20 minutter.
Skjær gulroten i terninger, legg i en liten bolle med en skvett vann og dekk til. Forkok i mikroen i 2 minutter på full styrke, til den så vidt er myk.
